referenceName: Independent mobile veterinarian with service rows and at-home visit emphasis

source.name: Perry Paws Mobile official website
source.sourceType: official direct veterinary-business website, captured in Playwright Chromium
source.rightsEvidence: Requester-attested clearance on 2026-09-29 covers retaining the paired desktop/mobile full-page captures, deriving a design prompt, and using these captures as internal pipeline-model visual references. No source-owner grant was supplied.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: An independent mobile practice places a compact brand-and-booking header over a spacious warm-neutral opening. The desktop promise is paired with a rounded at-home-care photograph, but all key service and geographic context remains separate, so the text is easy to scan. A contrasting reassurance statement breaks the hero, then a titled service index uses thin ruled rows and directional links instead of icon cards. A pale testimonial chapter contains compact text proof and two pet photographs, ending with a dark green footer that repeats the practical visit action, hours, and coverage. On mobile the promise comes first, then the image and service lines become an orderly single-column sequence. Transfer this direct, personal information hierarchy without the source identity, photo, exact wording, reviews, rate details, or claims.

heroGeometry.mode: copy-first at-home service opening beside one large rounded documentary image
heroGeometry.viewport: headline, one-sentence scope, and visit action fit in the opening viewport

navigationGeometry.mode: compact wordmark, plain topic links, and one pill booking action
navigationGeometry.mobile: minimal brand row and menu control followed by a visible booking link

typography.scale: fluid but restrained heading and short row labels

palette.contrastIntent: calm surfaces, readable paragraphs, and dark text on every button

imageTreatment.mode: one personal home-visit photo and a small pair of pet portraits
imageTreatment.crop: rounded large desktop crop with subject-centered mobile placement
imageTreatment.focalPoint: keep the pet and caregiver together without overlaying service text

servicePresentation.pattern: two-column ruled service index on desktop, full-width labeled service rows on mobile
servicePresentation.interaction: each row has a directional link and brief independent explanation

ctaPlacement.early: primary action sits alongside the opening promise

motion.primitive: quiet link feedback and responsive menu disclosure
motion.reducedMotion: keep content fully visible and remove nonessential transitions

mobileRecomposition.strategy: move headline, promise, and action first, then stack the hero image and thin service rows
rules: show service-area qualifications near the action
allow service descriptions to wrap without truncation
keep pet imagery after the promise rather than before it
do not pin an overlapping action rail

prohibitedPatterns: claiming the new client offers mobile or in-home visits without proof
using Perry Paws logo, photos, domain, testimonials, certifications, exact copy, hours, prices, or coverage
reproducing the source color scheme as a fixed brand identity
turning each service into a decorative card

requiredSignatureElements.description: A clear at-home or in-clinic service promise precedes the hero image and identifies who the practice helps.
Core services appear as clean rows with a short scope statement and useful destination.
Coverage is stated accurately and the next step clarifies how an address or service-area fit is confirmed.

acceptanceChecks: The first viewport explains the real service model and one next step.
The service list is scannable without repeated cards.
Coverage is based on submitted or verified facts and does not imply a clinic address.
Mobile action and all service descriptions fit without horizontal overflow.
Testimonials, fear-free credentials, prices, and health claims are not borrowed from the source.

review.notes: Official site returned HTTP 200 at both requested viewports. It identifies an active mobile veterinary practice in the Washington, DC service area. Full-page desktop and mobile images were visually checked; no broken content images or browser page errors were recorded.
